# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

＃179화



진짜 원단이네.

태원진가에서 출발하기 전, 위팽으로부터 신신당부를 들었던 것이 고작 이틀 전인데 까맣게 잊고 있었다.

헛숨을 삼킨 혁무진이 말했다.

“어, 어떡하죠?”

“어떡하긴 뭘 어떡해. 어차피 알고 있었어도 제시간에 못 맞췄을 텐데.”

다른 사람도 아니고 무려 화왕이다. 어제 분위기를 감안해 봤을 때, 집안일이 있어 이만 가 보겠다고 했으면 호쾌하게 보내 줬을 거다.

물론 집이 아니라 황천길로.

“위 대협께서 절 죽이실 겁니다.”

나는 안색이 거무죽죽해진 혁무진의 어깨를 두드려 주었다.

“괜찮아. 난 못 죽일걸.”

“오, 저도요!”

“…….”

이게 바로 뒷배 없는 자의 서러움이지.

하지만 굳이 늑장 부릴 생각은 없다.

명색이 태원진가가 산서성의 지배자로 우뚝 서는 날인데 그 집안 막내가 늦어서야 쓰나.

“짐 챙겨. 바로 출발한다.”

짐이라고 해 봤자 행낭 하나가 전부지만.

순식간에 준비를 끝마친 우리는 1층으로 내려갔다. 원단을 맞아 온통 붉게 장식된 객잔 안은 이른 아침임에도 불구하고 사람들로 북적거렸다.

그리고 그들 중, 유난히 눈에 띄는 두 사람이 있었다.

“오, 지금 일어났나?”

“쯧쯧. 젊은 놈들이 저렇게 잠이 많아서야.”

“그러게 말입니다. 저 젊을 적에는 하루 한 시진도 못 자는 날이 허다했는데.”

“한 시진이나? 이보게, 나 때는 말이야…….”

손을 들어 알은척하더니 이내 자기들끼리 술잔을 주고받는 두 노인.

벌겋게 달아오른 얼굴과 옆에 놓인 술동이는 낮부터 거하게 한 잔 걸쳤다는 증거다.

뒤따라 내려오던 혁무진이 작은 목소리로 속삭였다.

“저게 무슨 조합입니까?”

“나도 몰라.”

한 명은 어지간한 장정보다 몸집이 큰 거구의 노인이고, 다른 한 명은 입김을 불면 날아갈 것 같은 왜소한 체격이다.

화왕이야 그렇다치고.

‘장태보, 저 양반은 언제 왔대?’

의뢰 때문에 온 건가?

어쨌건 각자의 분야에서 일가(一家)를 이룬 두 노인은 어느샌가 꽤 친해진 듯 보였다.

“분위기 어수선한데 그냥 슬쩍 나가면 안 됩니까?”

“슬쩍 같은 소리 하네. 너 어제 오리 뼈로 얻어맞고 기절한 거 기억 안 나냐?”

“그게 오리 뼈였어요? 젠장, 어쩐지 골이 울리더라.”

“모른 척하고 나갔다가는 골이 빠개질걸.”

“그건 좀.”

“어때, 도망칠래?”

혁무진이 침울한 얼굴로 한숨을 내쉬었다.

“후우, 새해 첫날부터 재수 옴 붙었네.”

백번 공감한다. 새해 첫날 아침부터 화왕 적천강을 만나고 싶은 사람은 어디에도 없을 테니까.

“할아버지들, 만두 없어요?”

“고기도 많이 있다. 먹어라.”

“와아!”

……저놈 빼고.

나와 혁무진은 도살장에 끌려가는 소처럼 무거운 마음으로 걸음을 옮겼다.

빛의 속도로 음식들을 쑤셔 넣고 있던 청풍이 해맑게 웃으며 접시들을 내밀었다.

“으이! 마이어으! 드스 브스으!”

“……너나 많이 드세요.”

“즈 므그스느드!”

이런 녀석이 절정 고수라니. 이 불공평한 현실에 통탄을 금하지 못하겠다.

무림의 앞날을 걱정하던 내게 장태보가 말을 건넸다.

“그래, 자네들은 이제 어찌할 셈인가?”

“우선 본가로 돌아갈 생각입니다. 일이 좀 있어서요.”

“아, 그렇군. 태원진가에서 회합이 있다고 했나?”

현재 산서성 내에서 태원진가에 관한 일거수일투족은 뜨거운 감자다.

늙은 호랑이 취급받던 태원진가가 오랜 세월 끝에 산서 무림이라는 옥좌(玉座)에 다시 앉게 되었으니, 그 관심과 기대가 보통이 아닐 만도 했다.

장가촌 같은 조그마한 마을에서 집돌이 생활을 하는 장태보마저 알고 있을 정도니까.

“근래에 사람들이 모이기만 하면 그 얘기더군. 무림과는 하등 관련도 없는 양민들까지 눈요기한다고 몰려갈 정도니 말 다 했지.”

“설마 그렇게까지 올까요.”

“진수성찬에는 온갖 잡다한 것들이 끼어드는 법이지. 산서성이 제아무리 변방에 속한다지만 일성의 패주(霸主)가 되는 자리일세. 내 비록 무림인은 아니지만 보고 들은 경륜은 제법 되니 기대해 보게. 아, 그리고…….”

장태보가 낮은 목소리로 한마디를 덧붙였다.

“의뢰에 관해서는 걱정일랑 하지 말고.”

의뢰. 그 말을 듣자 문득 생각나는 것이 있었다.

당시에는 겨를이 없어 미처 묻지 못한 말이다.

“저기, 혹시 따로 필요하거나 그런 건 없으세요?”

“뭘 말인가?”

“여러 가지가 있지 않겠습니까.”

동네 세탁소에 가도 수선비를 주는데, 장태보는 천하에서 이름 높은 장인이다. 비록 현역 때만큼은 아니겠지만 그 실력이 십 년 동안 증발했다고는 생각하지 않는다.

그럼 분명 그만한 대가가 있어야 할 텐데…….

내 말뜻을 알아차린 장태보가 흰 수염을 쓸었다.

“사례를 하겠다. 뭐 그런 건가?”

“솔직히 말씀드려서 기대하시는 것만큼은 못 해 드립니다.”

“그럼 만 냥만 주게.”

만 냥이면 은자 백 냥이다. 분명 엄청난 거금이지만 그의 명성을 감안하면 특가 할인이나 다름없게 느껴졌다.

나는 시원하게 고개를 끄덕였다. 어차피 내 돈도 아닌데 뭐.

“준비해서 자택으로 보내 드리겠습니다.”

“은자 만 냥을? 태원 진가 기둥뿌리를 죄다 뽑아야겠구먼.”

“……은자로 만 냥이요?”

“당연하지. 내 몸값이 그렇게 싸구려로 보였나?”

“그럼 자그마치 백만 냥인데.”

“자그마치가 아니라 겨우 백만 냥이지. 천하제일의 신병이기를 얻을 수 있는데 그깟 재물이 대수인가?”

“…….”

당연히 대수지.

백만 냥이면 현실에서 얼마야, 수천억? 아니면 조 단위?

내 표정을 본 장태보가 피식 웃으며 입을 열었다.

“필요 없네.”

“죄송하지만 혹시 만 냥으로 쿨거래 가능하십니…… 예?”

“필요 없다고. 내가 그거 받아서 뭐 하겠나? 죽을 때까지 다 쓰지도 못할 텐데. 살아생전 이런 기회가 온 것만으로도 충분해.”

이런 것이 바로 장인 정신인가?

그야말로 빛태보. 천하의 야장들은 그를 본받아 태보해야 한다.

내가 감동으로 몸을 부르르 떨고 있던 그때 혁무진이 존경스럽다는 표정으로 끼어들었다.

“그럼 일단 만 냥만 받으시고 그거 저 주시면 안 됩니까?”

저 새끼는 자서전 써도 될 것 같다. 제목은 [맞아 뒤지는 방법 100선].

놈의 뒤통수를 후려친 나는 장태보에게 공손히 고개를 숙였다.

“그럼 모쪼록 부탁드립니다.”

“부탁은 내가 해야지. 기간이 얼마나 걸릴지는 장담하기 힘들지만, 분명 세상을 떨어 울릴 만한 물건이 나올 걸세. 그러니 부디 그때까지 그에 걸맞은 힘과 자격을 갖춰 주게.”

“노력하겠습니다.”

“그래, 그럼 된 거지. 자네를 믿어 보는 수밖에.”

고개를 끄덕이던 장태보가 멈칫했다.

“아. 그리고 하나만 부탁해도 되겠나?”

“……?”

“집 좀 다시 지어 주게. 죄다 불에 타서 잠잘 곳도 없어.”

은퇴 후 장만한 집. 편안한 노후를 보내던 소중한 공간이 하루아침에 사라졌다.

장태보의 서글픈 목소리에 시선이 저절로 옆을 향했다. 우리가 대화를 나누는 동안 조용히 술잔을 꺾고 있던 적천강이 눈을 치켜뜬다.

“뭘 봐.”

지난밤의 감성적이고 진지하던 적천강의 모습은 찾아볼 수 없다. 나는 슬쩍 시선을 회피했다.

“……아무것도 아닙니다.”

“할 말 있으면 해라. 노부는 그리 속 좁은 사람이 아니다.”

“진짜 해도 됩니까?”

It really was New Year’s Day.

It had only been two days since Wipeng had given me strict instructions before I left the Jin Family of Taiyuan, yet I had completely forgotten.

It had only been two days since Wipeng had given me strict instructions before I left the Jin Family of Taiyuan, yet I had completely forgotten.

Hyuk Mujin swallowed a hollow breath and spoke.

“W-What do we do?”

“What do you mean, what do we do? Even if we’d remembered, we wouldn’t have made it back in time.”

This was the Fire King we were talking about.

Considering the mood yesterday, if I’d told him I had family business and needed to leave, he would have sent me off with a hearty laugh.

Straight down the road to the underworld, of course.

“Great Hero Wipeng is going to kill me.”

I patted the ashen-faced Hyuk Mujin on the shoulder.

“Don’t worry. He can’t kill me.”

“Oh, me neither!”

“…”

Such was the sorrow of having no powerful backer.

Still, I had no intention of deliberately dragging my feet.

Today was the day the Jin Family of Taiyuan would rise as the undisputed ruler of Shanxi Province. The youngest son of the family couldn’t afford to be late.

“Pack your things. We’re leaving right now.”

Not that I had much to pack. One travel bundle was everything I owned.

“No idea.”

“Slip out, my ass. Don’t you remember getting knocked unconscious with a duck bone yesterday?”

“I’d rather avoid that.”

“So? Want to make a run for it?”

“There’s plenty of meat, too. Eat up.”

“Yaaay!”

Hyuk Mujin and I trudged forward with heavy hearts, like oxen being led to the slaughterhouse.

“Hewe! It’s delishush! Try shome!”

“…You eat plenty.”

“Thanksh, I will!”

Someone like him was a Peak master. The sheer unfairness of reality filled me with despair for the future of the Murim.

Jang Taebo spoke up.

“So, what are you all planning to do now?”

“We’re going back to our family first. We have some business to take care of.”

“Ah, I see. You said there was going to be a gathering at the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”

The Jin Family of Taiyuan, once treated as an old tiger past its prime, had reclaimed the throne of Shanxi Murim after many years. It was only natural that the interest and expectations surrounding them were extraordinary.

Even Jang Taebo, a homebody living in a tiny place like Jang Family Village, had heard about it.

“That’s all anyone talks about whenever people gather these days. Even ordinary people with nothing to do with the Murim are flocking there for the spectacle. That tells you everything.”

“Will that many people really come?”

“A grand feast always draws all sorts of hangers-on. Shanxi Province may be a frontier region, but this is about becoming the hegemon of an entire province. I may not be a martial artist, but I’ve seen and heard enough in my time. Just wait and see. Ah, and…”

Jang Taebo lowered his voice.

“Don’t worry about the commission.”

The commission.

His words suddenly reminded me of something I hadn’t had the chance to ask before.

“By the way, is there anything else you need?”

“What do you mean?”

“Well, there must be something.”

Even the neighborhood laundromat charged a fee for repairs. Jang Taebo was a master artisan renowned throughout the world. He might not have been as skilled as he was in his prime, but I didn’t believe his abilities had vanished over the past ten years.

His work had to command an appropriate price…

Realizing what I meant, Jang Taebo stroked his white beard.

“You mean you want to compensate me?”

“To be honest, I can’t give you as much as you might be expecting.”

“Then just give me ten thousand nyang.”

Ten thousand nyang was a hundred silver nyang. It was certainly an enormous sum, but considering his fame, it felt like nothing more than a special discount.

I nodded readily. It wasn’t my money, anyway.

“I’ll prepare it and send it to your home.”

“Ten thousand silver nyang? You’d have to tear out every last pillar holding up the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

“…Ten thousand *silver* nyang?”

“Of course. Did my worth look that cheap to you?”

“That’s a whopping million nyang.”

“Not a whopping million. A mere million. You’ll be getting the greatest divine weapon under heaven. What does a little money matter?”

“…”

Of course it mattered.

How much would a million nyang be worth in the real world? Hundreds of billions of won? Trillions?

Jang Taebo let out a quiet laugh at my expression.

“I don’t need it.”

“I’m sorry, but would you consider a quick deal for ten thousand nyang—pardon?”

“I said I don’t need it. What would I do with that much money? I couldn’t spend it all before I died. Having an opportunity like this come my way while I’m still alive is payment enough.”

Was this the spirit of a true artisan?

What a shining example, this Jang Taebo. Every blacksmith under heaven should follow his example and Taebo accordingly.

As I trembled with emotion, Hyuk Mujin cut in with an admiring look.

“Then why don’t you take the ten thousand nyang for now and give it to me?”

That bastard could write an autobiography. He could call it *A Hundred Ways to Get Yourself Beaten to Death*.

I smacked him on the back of the head, then bowed politely to Jang Taebo.

“Then I’ll leave it in your hands.”

“I’m the one who should be asking a favor. I can’t promise how long it will take, but I’ll create something that will make the world tremble. Until then, make sure you acquire the strength and qualifications worthy of wielding it.”

“I’ll do my best.”

“Good. Then that settles it. I’ll have to place my trust in you.”

Jang Taebo nodded, then paused.

“Ah. Could I ask one more favor?”

“…?”

“Build my house again. It all burned down, and I don’t even have anywhere to sleep.”

The home he had bought after retiring—the precious place where he had spent his golden years in peace—had vanished overnight.

At the sorrow in Jang Taebo’s voice, my gaze drifted to the side of its own accord.

Jeok Cheongang, who had been quietly sipping his wine while we talked, looked up.

“What are you staring at?”

There was no trace of the emotional, solemn Jeok Cheongang from last night. I subtly averted my gaze.

“…Nothing.”

“If you have something to say, say it. This old man isn’t so petty.”

“Are you really sure?”

“Go ahead.”

The moment he finished speaking, the space beneath the table began to heat up.

It wasn’t as though the innkeeper were a modern man who had brought in an electric heater…

*Fuck. Flame Divine Palm.*

Tears welled in my eyes as I answered.

“I was just thinking that you looked a good ten years younger than usual today.”

Jeok Cheongang frowned.

“What? Ten years?”

Damn it. Subtracting ten from a hundred still left ninety.

I hurriedly revised my answer.

“Twenty years…”

“Twenty years?”

“Thirty years…”

In the space of barely three seconds, Jeok Cheongang had grown thirty years younger. He nodded in satisfaction.

“I thought you were a fellow with nothing but shit in your head, but you do have some fairly plausible thoughts after all.”

“…”

Hyuk Mujin looked like he had something to say, but he clamped his mouth shut.

Apparently, he had no desire to make *A Hundred Ways to Get Yourself Beaten to Death* his final work.

Instead, he kept poking me in the side, looking desperate to leave this place immediately.

*Of course, I feel the same way.*

But before we could go, there was one last thing I needed to settle.

I spoke in the most respectful tone I could manage.

“I have several items in my possession.”

Jeok Cheongang, his face flushed as he tipped back his wine cup, let out a quiet laugh.

“Were you ever planning to return them?”

“Of course I did.”

“That’s right. If you don’t return them, you’ll see something ugly.”

“…”

The old man could see straight through people’s hearts like a ghost.

I forced a smile and placed the items I had already taken out on the table.

The Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual I had obtained from Jopil, and the Unnamed Sword made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

“As you already know, Great Hero Jeok, the Blazing Flame Divine Pill…”

“You gobbled it up.”

“Yes. That’s right.”

“But…”

A wrinkled finger tapped against the table. Jeok Cheongang continued in a dry voice.

“Where is the Treasured Jade?”

“Pardon?”

“The treasured jade. The jade.”

Treasured jade? As in some sort of treasure or gemstone?

Jeok Cheongang didn’t seem like the type to obsess over ordinary jewelry, so it had to be extremely important.

But since I hadn’t even known it existed, I could only stare at him in bewilderment.

“These are the only things I received.”

“Received? You didn’t collect them yourself?”

“No. There were circumstances. They were handed to me right after I woke up.”

“Do you suspect any of the people involved?”

Gong Yacheong and Socheon had handed Jopil’s belongings over to me. Neither of them was the sort to quietly pocket something behind everyone else’s back.

The same went for the members of the reconnaissance squad who had been there. I didn’t know what had happened, but that didn’t change my trust in them.

“They wouldn’t have. No, absolutely not.”

Jeok Cheongang studied me for a moment before speaking.

“Then it must be one of two things. Someone deceived you, or that child lost it.”

“…”

“What a nuisance. This has become troublesome.”

Jeok Cheongang had likely returned to the world not only to find his Disciple, but also to recover the Fire Gate Clan’s treasures that had been scattered because of him.

The Treasured Jade seemed to be one of them.

It was a treasure that even the Fire King was willing to endure the trouble of searching for at all costs.

*Damn it. I never even got to see it.*

Just as a creeping sense of danger began to outweigh my curiosity about what the jade actually was, Jeok Cheongang spoke.

“It can’t be helped. Keep them for now.”

That casual remark brought my thoughts to a complete halt.

Wait. Did he mean…

“You want me to keep these?”

“Yes.”

“Both of them?”

“All three. Have you forgotten the one in your stomach? Anything that originated from our sect must be reclaimed, one way or another.”

“…!”

“I’m joking.”

“Phew.”

“Tsk, tsk. You’re still young, but your nerve is already the size of a bean.”

Bean or cannonball, I didn’t care.

I wanted nothing more to do with that terrifying old man. Ever.

I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.

“I’m sorry, but I’ll have to decline—”

“If you refuse, I’ll reclaim them right now. All three.”

“…”

“This time, I’m serious.”

Once again, the space beneath the table grew scorching hot. There was no need to guess which technique it was.

*What the fuck?*

I was trying to return the items to their rightful owner. And I couldn’t even do that?

Overcome with resentment and indignation, I demanded, “Why are you doing this to me?”

“Do you expect an old man like me to carry those cumbersome things around? I don’t have the strength for that.”

“What if someone takes them from me?”

“Then this old man will kill you.”

“What if I learn the martial art?”

“Then you’ll die even more painfully.”

What kind of bullshit situation was this?

Leaving me standing there in a daze, the Fire King rose from his seat.

Cheongpung, who was still cramming food into his mouth, looked up.

“Gwandpa, awe you leaving?”

“…You’re even worse than your grandfather. Slow down.”

After exchanging a silent glance of farewell with Jang Taebo, Jeok Cheongang turned away and tossed out one meaningful remark.

“Let’s meet again soon.”

I didn’t want to see him.

Ever.

I spoke in the most respectful tone I could manage.

The Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual I had obtained from Jopil, and the Unnamed Sword made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

“Yes. That’s right.”

“But…”

“Where is the Treasured Jade?”

“Pardon?”

Treasured jade? As in some sort of treasure or gemstone?

“No. There were circumstances. They were handed to me right after I woke up.”

“They wouldn’t have. No, absolutely not.”

Jeok Cheongang studied me for a moment before speaking.

“Then it must be one of two things. Someone deceived you, or that child lost it.”

“…”

“What a nuisance. This has become troublesome.”

Jeok Cheongang had likely returned to the world not only to find his Disciple, but also to recover the Fire Gate Clan’s treasures that had been scattered because of him.

The Treasured Jade seemed to be one of them.

It was a treasure that even the Fire King was willing to endure the trouble of searching for at all costs.

*Damn it. I never even got to see it.*

Just as a creeping sense of danger began to outweigh my curiosity about what the jade actually was, Jeok Cheongang spoke.

“It can’t be helped. Keep them for now.”

That casual remark brought my thoughts to a complete halt.

Wait. Did he mean…

“You want me to keep these?”

“Yes.”

“Both of them?”

“All three. Have you forgotten the one in your stomach? Anything that originated from our sect must be reclaimed, one way or another.”

“…!”

“I’m joking.”

“Phew.”

“Tsk, tsk. You’re still young, but your nerve is already the size of a bean.”

Bean or cannonball, I didn’t care.

I wanted nothing more to do with that terrifying old man. Ever.

I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.

“I’m sorry, but I’ll have to decline—”

“If you refuse, I’ll reclaim them right now. All three.”

“…”

“This time, I’m serious.”

Once again, the space beneath the table grew scorching hot. It was Flame Divine Palm, of course.

*What the fuck?*

I was trying to return the items to their rightful owner. And I couldn’t even do that?

Overcome with resentment and indignation, I demanded, “Why are you doing this to me?”

“Do you expect an old man like me to carry those cumbersome things around? I don’t have the strength for that.”

“What if someone takes them from me?”

“Then this old man will kill you.”

“What if I learn the martial art?”

“Then you’ll die even more painfully.”

What kind of bullshit situation was this?

Leaving me standing there in a daze, the Fire King rose from his seat.

Cheongpung, who was still cramming food into his mouth, looked up.

“Gwandpa, awe you leaving?”

“…You’re even worse than your grandfather. Slow down.”

After exchanging a silent glance of farewell with Jang Taebo, Jeok Cheongang turned away and tossed out one meaningful remark.

“Let’s meet again soon.”

I didn’t want to see him.

Ever.

Straight down the road to the underworld, of course.

“Oh, me neither!”

Their flushed faces and the wine jar beside them showed they had already been drinking heavily this early in the day.

“No idea.”

One was a giant of an old man, larger than most strapping young men. The other was so small and frail that a stiff breeze might have carried him away.

The Fire King was one thing.

Had he come because of the commission?

“Slip out, my ass. Don’t you remember getting knocked unconscious with a duck bone yesterday?”

“That was a duck bone? Damn, no wonder my skull was ringing.”

“If we pretend nothing happened and leave, he’ll crack it open.”

“I’d rather avoid that.”

“So? Want to make a run for it?”

Hyuk Mujin sighed gloomily.

“Phew. What a rotten way to start the new year.”

I couldn’t have agreed more. No one in the world would want to run into Fire King Jeok Cheongang first thing on New Year’s Day.

“Grandpas, do you have any dumplings?”

“There’s plenty of meat, too. Eat up.”

“Yaaay!”

…Except that guy.

Hyuk Mujin and I trudged forward with heavy hearts, like oxen being led to the slaughterhouse.

Cheongpung, who was shoveling food into his mouth at the speed of light, beamed and held out several plates.

“Hewe! It’s delishush! Try shome!”

“…You eat plenty.”

“Thanksh, I will!”

Someone like him was a Peak master. The sheer unfairness of reality filled me with despair for the future of the Murim.

“So, what are you all planning to do now?”

“We’re going back to our family first. We have some business to take care of.”

“Ah, I see. You said there was going to be a gathering at the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
